title: Sharp maps: pullback criterion and cartesian-square calculus
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and the Kan--Quillen weak equivalences and functorial model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. A commutative square is homotopy cartesian if its upper-left corner maps by a weak equivalence to the homotopy pullback of its other corners, computed by fibrant replacement. Call $p:E\to B$ sharp if every strict pullback of $p$ along every small map $T\to B$ is homotopy cartesian.
Then $p$ is sharp if and only if, for every weak equivalence $u:A\to A'$ over $B$, the map $E\times_B A\to E\times_B A'$ is a weak equivalence. Sharp maps are stable under arbitrary base change. In particular $p\times\mathrm{id}_K:E\times K\to B\times K$ is sharp for every simplicial set $K$.
For a commutative square $E'\to E$ over $B'\to B$ with $p:E\to B$ sharp, that square is homotopy cartesian if and only if its canonical map $E'\to B'\times_B E$ is a weak equivalence. If $p':E'\to B'$ is also sharp and this square is homotopy cartesian, then for every $T\to B'$ the induced comparison $E'\times_{B'}T\to E\times_B T$ is a weak equivalence; equivalently, the induced square $E'\times_{B'}T\to E$ over $T\to B$ is homotopy cartesian. Consequently two horizontally adjacent homotopy-cartesian squares whose three vertical maps are sharp have homotopy-cartesian outer rectangle. Taking the product of such a square with any simplicial set $K$ preserves homotopy-cartesianness. In particular the square $E\times K\to E\times L$ over $B\times K\to B\times L$ is homotopy cartesian for any map $K\to L$ and any sharp $p$.

source.place: Section 2, definition of sharp maps; Proposition 2.7 and its proof, printed pp. 3-4, with the base-change and pasting consequences of the strict-pullback comparison criterion. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Fix a functorial fibrant replacement $r:\mathrm{id}\to R$ from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. By [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition], for every commutative square $Q\to X$ over $Y\to Z$, its homotopy-cartesianness is equivalent to the constant-path comparison $RQ\to RX\times_{RZ,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,RZ)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,RZ}RY$ being a weak equivalence. This supplies the explicit bridge to the Kan path model used in the pasting steps below.

source.place: Section 2, definition of homotopy-cartesian square (homotopy pullback via fibrant replacement in a right proper model category)

proof.text: For a strictly commuting map of square diagrams which is a weak equivalence at every corner, apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-cartesian-invariance]. It preserves and reflects homotopy-cartesianness even when the original corners are not Kan.

source.place: Section 2, definition of homotopy-cartesian square (homotopy pullback via fibrant replacement in a right proper model category)

proof.text: For a square over $X\to Z\xleftarrow{g}Y$ with $g$ a Kan fibration, [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-cartesian-fibration-criterion] says that it is homotopy cartesian exactly when the canonical map $Q\to X\times_ZY$ is a weak equivalence. Only the leg $g$, not the objects, is required to be fibrant.

source.place: Section 2, definition of homotopy-cartesian square (homotopy pullback via fibrant replacement in a right proper model category)

proof.text: For arbitrary $g:Y\to Z$, factor $g$ as $Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_f\to Z$ with the last map a Kan fibration, using [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. The induced map of squares is the identity on $Q,X,Z$ and the weak equivalence $Y\to Y_f$ on the fourth corner. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-cartesian-invariance] and then [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-cartesian-fibration-criterion]. Thus the original square is homotopy cartesian if and only if $Q\to X\times_ZY_f$ is a weak equivalence. This is just the two successive applications, with no additional comparison lemma.

source.place: Section 2, definition of homotopy-cartesian square (homotopy pullback via fibrant replacement in a right proper model category)

proof.text: Let $p:E\to B$ and first assume it is sharp. Let $u:A\to A'$ be a weak equivalence over $B$, with structure maps $a:A\to B$, $a':A'\to B$ and $a'u=a$. Factor $p$ as a weak equivalence $E\to E_f$ followed by a Kan fibration $E_f\to B$. The strict pullback squares of $p$ along $a$ and $a'$ are homotopy cartesian by sharpness, so by Step 4, applied with the factored leg $p$, the maps $E\times_BA\to E_f\times_BA$ and $E\times_BA'\to E_f\times_BA'$ are weak equivalences. The map $E_f\times_BA\to E_f\times_BA'$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance], applied to the map of cospans $(\mathrm{id}_{E_f},\mathrm{id}_B,u)$ whose legs $E_f\to B$ are Kan fibrations. The evident square of these four pullbacks commutes, so two-out-of-three gives that $E\times_BA\to E\times_BA'$ is a weak equivalence. Conversely assume that pullback along $p$ carries every weak equivalence over $B$ to a weak equivalence. For any $t:T\to B$ factor $t$ as a weak equivalence $T\to T_f$ followed by a Kan fibration $T_f\to B$. By hypothesis $E\times_BT\to E\times_BT_f$ is a weak equivalence, and by Step 4, applied with the factored leg $t$, this says exactly that the strict pullback square $E\times_BT\to E$ over $T\to B$ is homotopy cartesian. Hence $p$ is sharp. (Edge case: $u=\mathrm{id}$ gives the identity; $T=\varnothing$ gives empty pullbacks on both sides.)

Sharpness is stable under arbitrary base change. Let $g:B'\to B$ and $p':E'=E\times_BB'\to B'$. If $u:A\to A'$ is a weak equivalence over $B'$, composing the structure maps with $g$ makes it a weak equivalence over $B$, and $E'\times_{B'}A=E\times_BA$, $E'\times_{B'}A'=E\times_BA'$ canonically and compatibly with $u$. By the forward direction of Step 5 for $p$ the induced map is a weak equivalence, so by the converse direction of Step 5, $p'$ is sharp. Taking $g$ to be the projection $B\times K\to B$, whose pullback of $p$ is canonically $p\times\mathrm{id}_K:E\times K\to B\times K$, shows that $p\times\mathrm{id}_K$ is sharp for every simplicial set $K$ (including $K=\varnothing$).

Consider a commutative square $E'\to E$ over $B'\to B$ with $p:E\to B$ sharp, and put $P=B'\times_BE$ with its projection $q:P\to B'$. The square factors as the square $E'\to P$ over $\mathrm{id}_{B'}$ followed by the strict pullback square $P\to E$ over $B'\to B$, which is homotopy cartesian because $p$ is sharp. Apply the functorial replacement $R$ of Step 1 to this diagram of two adjacent strict squares; it consists of Kan complexes and strictly commuting squares, and by Step 1 each of the three squares (left, right, outer) is homotopy cartesian iff its $R$-image is a homotopy pullback in the path sense. The pasting criterion [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], with the right square a homotopy pullback, says the left $R$-square is a homotopy pullback iff the outer one is. So the original square is homotopy cartesian iff the square $E'\to P$ over $\mathrm{id}_{B'}$ is. The identity $\mathrm{id}_{B'}$ is a Kan fibration, so by Step 3 the latter square is homotopy cartesian iff $E'\to P\times_{B'}B'=P$, the canonical map, is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.7, comparison criterion for a square over a sharp map

proof.text: Assume also that $p':E'\to B'$ is sharp and that the square $E'\to E$ over $b:B'\to B$ is homotopy cartesian. Let $t:T\to B'$. The strict pullback square $E'\times_{B'}T\to E'$ over $t$ is homotopy cartesian because $p'$ is sharp. Paste it to the left of the given square: after the replacement $R$ of Step 1, [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] (right square a homotopy pullback, left square a homotopy pullback) makes the outer rectangle, i.e. the square $E'\times_{B'}T\to E$ over $bt:T\to B$, homotopy cartesian. Since $p$ is sharp, Step 7 applied to this outer square says this is equivalent to its canonical map $E'\times_{B'}T\to T\times_BE$ being a weak equivalence; this canonical map is the induced comparison of the statement. This proves both formulations and their equivalence.

source.place: Section 2, base-change and comparison consequences of Proposition 2.7

proof.text: Pasting: for two horizontally adjacent homotopy-cartesian squares (the hypothesis that the three vertical maps are sharp is not needed here), apply the replacement $R$ of Step 1 to the whole diagram and then [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting]; the outer $R$-rectangle is a homotopy pullback, so the outer rectangle is homotopy cartesian by Step 1. Products: let $E'\to E$ over $b:B'\to B$ be homotopy cartesian with $p,p'$ sharp, let $K$ be a simplicial set, and put $P=B'\times_BE$ with $q:P\to B'$. By Step 6, $q$ is sharp, and by Step 7 for the given square, $c:E'\to P$ is a weak equivalence. The square $c:E'\to P$ over $\mathrm{id}_{B'}$ has sharp vertical maps $p',q$ and is homotopy cartesian by Step 7 applied with the sharp map $q$ (its canonical map is $c$). Apply Step 8 to it with $T=B'\times K\to B'$ the projection: $c\times\mathrm{id}_K:E'\times K\to P\times K$ is a weak equivalence. Now $(B'\times K)\times_{B\times K}(E\times K)=P\times K$ canonically, with $c\times\mathrm{id}_K$ as the canonical map of the product square, and $p\times\mathrm{id}_K$ is sharp by Step 6; Step 7 therefore makes the product square homotopy cartesian.

source.place: Section 2, pasting and product consequences after Proposition 2.7

proof.text: Finally let $K\to L$ be any map and let $p:E\to B$ be sharp. By the base-change step, $p\times\mathrm{id}_L:E\times L\to B\times L$ is sharp. The displayed square $E\times K\to E\times L$ over $B\times K\to B\times L$ is the strict pullback of this sharp map along $B\times K\to B\times L$, with pullback object canonically $E\times K$. The definition of sharpness therefore makes this square homotopy cartesian.
